messages.content: Find the Net Present Value (NPV) of an investment, given cash_flows=[200,300,400,500], a discount rate of 10%, and an initial investment of $2000.

function.name: calculate_NPV
function.description: Calculate the NPV (Net Present Value) of an investment, considering a series of future cash flows, discount rate, and an initial investment. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

discount_rate.description: The discount rate to use. This is a float type value.

initial_investment.description: The initial investment. Default is 0 if not specified.

message.content:
The net present value (NPV) is calculated as  

\[
\text{NPV}= -\,I_0+\sum_{t=1}^{N}\frac{\text{CF}_t}{(1+r)^t}
\]

where  
\(I_0\) = \$2000 (initial out‑flow),  
\(r\) = 10 % = 0.10,  
and \(\text{CF}_t\) are the yearly inflows \(200,\;300,\;400,\;500\).

| Year | Cash Flow (\$) | Discount factor \((1+r)^t\) | Present value |
|------|-----------------|--------------------------------|---------------|
| 1    | 200             | 1.10                           | 200 ÷ 1.10   = **181.82** |
| 2    | 300             | 1.21                           | 300 ÷ 1.21   = **247.93** |
| 3    | 400             | 1.331                          | 400 ÷ 1.331  = **300.60** |
| 4    | 500             | 1.4641                         | 500 ÷ 1.4641 = **341.46** |

Total discounted inflow  
\[
\Sigma_{\text{PV}} = 181.82 + 247.93 + 300.60 + 341.46 \approx \$1\,071.81 .
\]

Finally,

\[
\boxed{
\text{NPV} = -2000 + 1071.81 \;\approx\; -\$928.20
}
\]

Hence the project has a negative NPV of roughly –$928, indicating that, under a 10 % discount rate, the expected returns fall short of covering the initial investment.
